commit.message:
Plugin 4: loop-designer — guarded autonomous loop generator

* feat: add loop-designer plugin — guarded autonomous loop generator

New plugin turning recurring tasks into guarded loops. Architecture
generalized from a production daily-radar Routine (Discover/Plan/
Execute/Verify/Stop with a file-based seen-log for cross-run memory)
plus prompt-optimizer-loop's locked-checklist discipline — documented
in references/loop-anatomy.md. references/guardrail-design.md states
the failure each of the five non-negotiable guardrails prevents.
Hard rules: all five guardrails always, executor never verifies its
own work, verification-first (no checkable success condition, no
loop), state lives in files, honest empty runs.

* feat: add loop-designer worked example — daily GitHub issue triage

sample-request.md shows the minimal interview including the
verification-first conversion of an underspecified goal into a
checkable success condition. sample-loop-package.md is the known-answer
output: five-part spec with a 5-item binary verifier checklist distinct
from the executor, the full numbered guardrails block, and both runner
artifacts (standalone Routine prompt + cron/launchd variant) with a
pick-one instruction. Doubles as the Gate 3 fixture.

* feat: register loop-designer in marketplace, add README and fixtures

README covers the four ways first loops fail (amnesia, unbounded
growth, silent death, self-graded output) and how the guardrails make
each structurally unavoidable. Fixtures follow the three-gate
convention, including the prompt-optimizer-loop routing-away case, a
skip-the-verifier refusal case, and a no-success-condition refusal
case. marketplace.json now lists four plugins.

* fix: route built-in /loop overlap out of loop-designer triggers

/pr-review flagged that "run this on a schedule" phrasings could also
mean the built-in /loop command's job (run something on an interval in
the current session). Adds explicit routing to the Do-NOT clause —
loop-designer designs durable guarded loops, it doesn't run them — plus
the matching NO-FIRE fixture case and a README note.

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: narrow cli-over-mcp-auditor trigger to avoid mcp-migration-auditor collision

PR #5 review flagged that the bare "audit my MCPs" phrasing routes
unqualified audit requests to the context-cost skill even when the
user means spec compatibility. Narrows the phrasing to "audit my MCPs
for context cost", adds a Do-NOT line routing spec-compatibility and
migration audits to mcp-migration-auditor, updates the trigger
fixtures both directions, and bumps pm-tactical to 0.2.1.

commit.message:
Plugin 3: mcp-migration-auditor — 2026-07-28 spec readiness scanner

* feat: add mcp-migration-auditor plugin with source-verified audit rules

New plugin auditing MCP configs against the 2026-07-28 specification
release candidate. Six audit rules (session dependency, handshake
pinning, deprecated roots/sampling/logging, experimental Tasks, OAuth
hardening, stdio all-clear), each tracing to a quoted official source
in references/spec-changes.md — the official MCP blog RC announcement
and spec changelog, with SEP numbers (2567, 2575, 2577, 2596, 2663,
2468, 2352, 837, 2164) and URLs. Hard rules forbid invented audit
rules, false alarms on stdio-only setups, and guessing capabilities a
config cannot show.

* feat: add sample vulnerable config and known-answer audit output

sample-mcp-config.json carries the three test archetypes: a stateful
HTTP server (Mcp-Session-Id header + session-store note), a stdio
server using MCP sampling, and a clean stdio server.
sample-audit-output.md records the expected audit — BREAKS (SEP-2567),
DEGRADED (SEP-2577 with the SEP-2596 12-month clock), SAFE — with the
prioritized deadline-framed checklist and evidence-honesty notes.
Doubles as the Gate 3 fixture.

* feat: register mcp-migration-auditor in marketplace, add README and fixtures

README is a standalone landing page (problem, install, 60-second usage
with sample output table, source-cited rule list).
tests/mcp-migration-auditor/fixtures.md follows the repo's three-gate
convention, including a no-false-alarm all-clear case and a
no-cross-contamination expectation. marketplace.json now lists all
three plugins.

---------

commit.message:
Plugin 2: pm-verifier — spec-to-eval-harness engine

* feat: add pm-verifier plugin with eval-engine skill

New plugin turning any feature spec into a verification layer. The
eval-engine SKILL.md (93 lines, lint-clean) produces three artifacts:
binary disqualifying gates with per-gate WHY lines, a calibrated 1-5
LLM-judge rubric with anchors and worked examples, and a runnable
harness scaffold. Gate-vs-rubric distinction stated up front; deep
guidance split into references/gate-design.md (gate test, canonical
families, gate smells) and references/rubric-calibration.md (anchor
design, judge prompt, human-vs-judge disagreement as calibration
signal).

* feat: add pure-stdlib eval harness templates (prepare/run/report)

prepare.py validates cases/ JSON and rejects malformed cases with
named-field errors. run.py applies mechanical gates in code first —
any failure finalizes the case as FAIL with rubric scoring skipped —
then routes judge gates and rubric scores through the user's own
Claude session via generated judgments/<id>.prompt.md files picked up
on re-run. report.py renders a pass/fail table, per-criterion 1-5
histograms, and a judge-assigned-not-objective caveat. No API keys,
no network, stdlib only.

* feat: add worked example — ticket-summarizer spec through eval-engine

examples/sample-spec.md (AI summarizes customer support tickets) plus
examples/sample-eval/ holding the skill's full output for it: 5 gates
(4 mechanical, 1 judge fabrication gate), 5-criterion rubric with
feature-specific anchors, self-contained judge prompt, 2 test cases
(one clean, one failing the commitment-language gate), and a filled
judgment showing the round-trip format. Doubles as the Gate 3
end-to-end fixture.

commit.message:
feat: v0.2.0 — make pm-tactical proactive across the plugin

* feat: v0.2.0 — make pm-tactical proactive across the plugin

Single concern: trigger redesign so skills act on observed session
state instead of waiting for explicit requests.

- model-complexity-router: fires on any substantial task handoff, not
  just direct model questions; scores silently and emits one compact
  header line (full breakdown preserved for direct asks); fires once
  per distinct task.
- cli-over-mcp-auditor: new first-prompt check inspects the session's
  own connected MCPs with no user-pasted list required, emits one line
  only when connectors look unused for the task at hand; explicit
  deep-audit flow unchanged.
- pm-context-system: replaces the upfront 5-question interview with
  observe-and-propose — one-line "Log to memory" proposals tied to
  decisions/facts as they happen, silent scaffold on first yes.
- builder-validator: freezes the spec silently (audit result only is
  shown) and adds a hard rule against inventing gate-critical facts —
  stops to ask the user instead of fabricating dates/names/numbers.
- CLAUDE.md: adds a session header protocol so the three proactive
  checks combine into one compact (max 4 line) header on the first
  substantial prompt, staying silent when a check has nothing to say.
- plugin.json bumped to 0.2.0; test fixtures updated to cover
  proactive firing (plain task handoffs, no-paste MCP inspection,
  propose-not-interview, missing-fact refusal).

* docs: fix session header protocol conflict with per-skill firing rules

/pr-review caught that CLAUDE.md's "once per session" framing
contradicted model-complexity-router's per-task and pm-context-system's
per-decision firing rules in their own SKILL.md files. Clarifies the
header as a first-prompt formatting convenience only — each skill
keeps firing independently afterward per its own rules; only
cli-over-mcp-auditor's check is genuinely one-time.

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
docs: add CLAUDE.md skill-routing fallback and README constraint note

* docs: add CLAUDE.md web-fallback skill routing and README constraint note

pm-tactical plugin skills auto-fire on CLI/desktop but not in Claude Code
web sessions. Adds an explicit routing table to CLAUDE.md so web sessions
can manually follow the matching SKILL.md, and documents the constraint
in README so it isn't rediscovered as a bug.

* docs: correct web-fallback claim after retest — native fire works once settings are committed

Retesting after PR #1 merged showed pm-tactical firing natively in this
same session, contradicting the earlier CLI-vs-web framing. Corrects
CLAUDE.md and README to describe the real gap: sessions predating the
committed .claude/settings.json, or with a mid-session-only install,
won't have the plugin in their invocable set yet.

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
